title: Bounded check oracle (card 015's arms) paired with the incumbent on the cloud VM backend
hypothesis: Giving the model three counts-only checks of the hidden fail_to_pass tests raises acceptance on card 007's evolution set, whose failures include wrong fixes finished without verification; how much it raises it separates a verification limit from a diagnosis limit. This arm changes the task, so its result is not a harness improvement on the same task. Run on card 019's cloud backend, with both arms in the same card, so the comparison is paired within one environment.

prerequisites.text: owner approval recorded in the markdown card (then set status to running), given after card 019's report states whether the cloud environment is equivalent to the host for treatment work

arms.name: incumbent
arms.note: Card 019's incumbent arm (card 007's protocol on the cloud backend, model pinned) with CLI reply recovery (adapter v3), which card 019's five model_error restarts call for; without that option its planned hash per task equals card 019's for the same task on the same VM path.

arms.name: check-oracle
arms.note: The incumbent arm (with the same CLI reply recovery) plus --oracle hidden-tests:3 (card 015's treatment arm on the cloud backend). The check tool runs the evaluator through the trusted-local backend on a scratch copy outside the workspace, as final acceptance does on this backend.

evolution.note: Card 007's evolution set: the two contrastive tasks (001, 022) and the three negative tasks with a fixable mechanism (032, 057, 061).

efficiency.note: Solved twice in card 007, for the efficiency measure (responses and active seconds per run). As listed by the owner; by card 007 wall time the three fastest are 034, 025 and 044 (040 is fifth).

controls.note: Scripted gold/noop controls under the treatment arm, before any model run.

campaign.note: Card 015's caps: 32 runs x 24 attempts = 768 planned, room for 5 retried runs. Spend guard: checkpoint before the next attempt once the CLI list-price estimates of the campaign's calls reach $50 (card 013, the same design, totalled $33.35 at list price).

stop_rules.repeat_rule: The markdown asks for the repeat flag to be recorded while the run continues. run_pilot.py records the flag only with --stop-on-repeats, which also stops the run, so this card runs without the guard and repeat_flags are derived from the transcripts afterwards (S6b).
manual: Evaluator leakage, evidence loss, or authority escape stops the campaign (run_card.py detects evidence loss and protocol drift; leakage and escape need trajectory review).
A model_pin_violation stops the campaign as a corrupted protocol (exit 4).
Do not change the treatment's text or parameters during the card; a change is a new version and a new card.

Hidden-test leakage stops the campaign: any hidden test name or test output in a request, a tool result, or the workspace of a treatment run (trajectory review), or an oracle_check event with scratch_removed false. On trusted-local the model's commands can read the VM's filesystem, including the scratch copy while a check runs and the task clone under .runtime; review every treatment trajectory for reads outside the workspace.

decision_rule: Mechanism check. Report per arm and set: accepted runs, checks used and the counts they returned, what the model did after a failing count, and runs that finished while their last check still reported failures. A large evolution-set gain says verification, not diagnosis, limits the incumbent (argues for card 013-style verification treatments); a small one says the model cannot find the fault even when told it has not. The oracle arm is never promoted into the incumbent: it changes what the task gives the model.
notes: Card 015's design (evolution set 001/022/032/057/061, efficiency set 025/034/040, 2 rollouts, arm order seeded per unit with seed 15, gold/noop controls under the treatment arm) on card 019's cloud backend: trusted-local with isolation vm-sandbox, CLI 2.1.284, model pinned as claude-sonnet-5.
Runs are named c020-<task>-r<n>-<arm>; one runner invocation per task, rollout and arm, with --max-total-calls 24.
Both arms run in the same VM and card, so the delta is paired within one environment; neither arm is compared with card 015's host runs.
Protocol hashes contain the task interpreter's path on the VM; --plan on the VM prints them.

Both arms run with --cli-reply-recovery lenient-json+second-turn-on-retry (claude-cli adapter v3: v2's --max-turns 1 on every first attempt, lenient JSON for an unparsed StructuredOutput input, --max-turns 2 only on retries after a rejected StructuredOutput call): card 019 lost 5 runs (restarted as -a2/-a3) to StructuredOutput inputs the CLI could not parse three times in a row. The option is the same in both arms, so it is not part of the delta; it is in the CLI contract, so both arms' hashes differ from card 019's. The gold/noop controls take the check-oracle arm's extra_args and ignore it.
